title: Adjoining a variable with a prescribed cycle as differential
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $(B,d,\gamma)$ be a divided-power differential graded $R$-algebra [def-sfb-divided-power-dga], let $e\geq1$, and let $z\in B_{e-1}$ satisfy $d(z)=0$. Let $C=B\langle T\rangle$ be the graded divided-power algebra obtained by adjoining one variable $T$ of degree $e$ as in [lem-sfb-divided-power-variable-adjunction]: exterior if $e$ is odd, and divided-power if $e$ is even. There exists a unique differential $D:C_q\to C_{q-1}$ extending $d$ on $B$, compatible with the divided-power structure on $C$, and satisfying $D(T)=z$, such that $(C,D,\gamma)$ is a divided-power differential graded $R$-algebra. In particular $B\hookrightarrow C$ is a morphism of divided-power differential graded algebras. Explicitly, for homogeneous $b\in B$, $D(bT)=d(b)T+(-1)^{\deg(b)}bz$ if $e$ is odd; if $e$ is even, writing $T^{[a]}=\gamma_a(T)$, one has $D(bT^{[a]})=d(b)T^{[a]}+(-1)^{\deg(b)}bzT^{[a-1]}$ for every $a\geq1$.

source.place: Tag 09PM (lemma-extend-differential), the differential extension on the single-variable graded divided-power algebra; explicit formulas from the Leibniz and divided-power differential rules

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-divided-power-variable-adjunction] on the underlying graded divided-power algebra of $B$ [def-sfb-divided-power-dga]. It supplies $C$ with its strict graded commutativity, extended divided powers, and free left $B$-module basis $1,T$ in odd degree, or $t_a=T^{[a]}$ for $a\geq0$ in even degree. Define an $R$-linear map on the direct-sum components by $D(b)=d(b)$ and $D(bT)=d(b)T+(-1)^p bz$ in the odd case; in the even case put $D(bt_a)=d(b)t_a+(-1)^p bz t_{a-1}$ for $a\geq1$ and $D(bt_0)=d(b)$. Here $b\in B_p$. These are well-defined formulas on the free summands, not prescriptions on an algebra presentation. Every term has degree $\deg(bt_a)-1$ (or $\deg(bT)-1$), since $\deg z=e-1$. Finite sums define $D$ on all of $C$; degree zero maps to zero. In particular $D|_B=d$ and $D(T)=z$.

source.place: Tag 09PM (lemma-extend-differential), omitted direct computation; using Tags 09PH/09PI (example-adjoining-odd/even) and 09PJ (definition-divided-powers-dga).

proof.text: Check the signed Leibniz rule in the odd case using the multiplication from [lem-sfb-divided-power-variable-adjunction] and the old Leibniz rule from [def-sfb-divided-power-dga]. By bilinearity only pairs $b,c$, $b,cT$, $bT,c$, $bT,cT$, with $b\in B_p,c\in B_q$, need checking. The first is the old rule. For the second, both sides are $d(bc)T+(-1)^{p+q}bc z$. For the third, using $(bT)c=(-1)^qbcT$, both sides are $(-1)^q d(b)cT+(-1)^{p+q}b d(c)T+(-1)^pbc z$. For the fourth the product is zero, and the right side is $(-1)^pbc zT+(-1)^{p+1}bc zT=0$: the terms with two $T$ factors vanish. Here $z$ is even, so $zc=cz$ and $Tz=zT$. These calculations prove the rule on all homogeneous elements of $C$.

source.place: Tag 09PM (lemma-extend-differential), omitted direct computation; using Tags 09PH/09PI (example-adjoining-odd/even) and 09PJ (definition-divided-powers-dga).

proof.text: Check the even-case Leibniz rule on $bt_a,ct_s$ with $b\in B_p,c\in B_q$ using [lem-sfb-divided-power-variable-adjunction] and [def-sfb-divided-power-dga]. Their product is $\binom{a+s}{a}bc t_{a+s}$. The coefficient of $t_{a+s}$ in each side of the rule is $\binom{a+s}{a}(d(b)c+(-1)^pb d(c))$. If $a+s>0$, the coefficient of $bc zt_{a+s-1}$ on the left is $(-1)^{p+q}\binom{a+s}{a}$; on the right it is $(-1)^{p+q}(\binom{a+s-1}{a-1}+\binom{a+s-1}{a})$, which is equal by Pascal's identity. In the first term of the right side, moving $z$ past $c$ contributes $(-1)^q$, because $z$ is odd. Omit the first binomial when $a=0$ and the second when $s=0$; these boundary cases give the same equality. If $a=s=0$ this is just the old Leibniz rule. Bilinearity finishes the check.

source.place: Tag 09PM (lemma-extend-differential), omitted direct computation; using Tags 09PH/09PI (example-adjoining-odd/even) and 09PJ (definition-divided-powers-dga).

proof.text: Verify $D^2=0$ directly. On $B$ it is $d^2=0$ from [def-sfb-divided-power-dga]. In the odd case, applying the defining formula twice to $bT$ gives $d^2(b)T+((-1)^{p-1}+(-1)^p)d(b)z+b d(z)=0$. If $p=0$, terms involving $d(b)$ are zero. In the even case and $a\geq1$ the result is $d^2(b)t_a+((-1)^{p-1}+(-1)^p)d(b)z t_{a-1}+b d(z)t_{a-1}-b z^2t_{a-2}$, with the last term absent for $a=1$. The first three terms vanish; the last vanishes because $z$ has odd degree $e-1$ and odd squares vanish strictly, including in characteristic two. This proves the claim on the free summands and hence everywhere. No assertion about ordinary graded commutativity alone is used to deduce odd squares zero.

source.place: Tag 09PM (lemma-extend-differential), omitted direct computation; using Tags 09PH/09PI (example-adjoining-odd/even) and 09PJ (definition-divided-powers-dga).

proof.text: For even $e$, first verify divided-power compatibility on a monomial $bt_a$ of positive even degree, where $a\geq1$ and $b$ is homogeneous even. By [lem-sfb-divided-power-variable-adjunction], $\gamma_n(bt_a)=K_{n,a}b^nt_{na}$, where $K_{n,a}=(na)!/(n!(a!)^n)$ and set $K_{0,a}=1$. Using the Leibniz rule already checked, $D\gamma_n(bt_a)=nK_{n,a}b^{n-1}d(b)t_{na}+K_{n,a}b^nz t_{na-1}$. On multiplying $D(bt_a)$ by $\gamma_{n-1}(bt_a)$, the two respective coefficients are $K_{n-1,a}\binom{na}{a}$ and $K_{n-1,a}\binom{na-1}{a-1}$. They equal $nK_{n,a}$ and $K_{n,a}$: substitute the factorial expressions and cancel factorials as integer identities. Thus no integer is inverted in $R$. This holds also when $n=1$. For $a=0$ and $b$ positive even it is exactly the old compatibility from [def-sfb-divided-power-dga].

source.place: Tag 09PM (lemma-extend-differential), omitted direct computation; using Tags 09PH/09PI (example-adjoining-odd/even) and 09PJ (definition-divided-powers-dga).

proof.text: The preceding even-case check extends to every positive even element by the divided-power addition formula in [def-sfb-divided-power-dga], valid in $C$ by [lem-sfb-divided-power-variable-adjunction]. Explicitly, if compatibility holds for $u,v$ for all indices, differentiate $\gamma_n(u+v)=\sum_{i+j=n}\gamma_i(u)\gamma_j(v)$. Every factor $\gamma_i(u)$ has even parity, so the Leibniz rule gives $\sum_{i+j=n,i>0}D(u)\gamma_{i-1}(u)\gamma_j(v)+\sum_{i+j=n,j>0}D(v)\gamma_i(u)\gamma_{j-1}(v)=(D(u)+D(v))\gamma_{n-1}(u+v)$. The derivative of $\gamma_0=1$ is zero. Each element of $C_{\mathrm{even},+}$ is a finite sum of the monomials checked in the preceding step, including a positive even constant coefficient; induction on that finite sum proves compatibility. This is just a reindexing of finite sums, not an appeal to a separate compatibility theorem.

source.place: Tag 09PM (lemma-extend-differential), omitted direct computation; using Tags 09PH/09PI (example-adjoining-odd/even) and 09PJ (definition-divided-powers-dga).

proof.text: For odd $e$, take any positive even element $w=x+yT$, with $x\in B_{\mathrm{even},+}$ and $y\in B_{\mathrm{odd}}$. The formula of [lem-sfb-divided-power-variable-adjunction] gives $\gamma_n(w)=\gamma_n(x)+\gamma_{n-1}(x)yT$. For $n\geq2$, differentiating this expression using the old compatibility [def-sfb-divided-power-dga] gives $d(x)\gamma_{n-1}(x)+d(x)\gamma_{n-2}(x)yT+\gamma_{n-1}(x)d(y)T-\gamma_{n-1}(x)yz$. Expanding $D(w)\gamma_{n-1}(w)$ gives the same four terms: the other two terms vanish, one because it contains two $T$ factors, and the other because $yzyT=zy^2T=0$. Indeed $z$ is even, and $y^2=0$ even if $y$ is inhomogeneous: expand into finitely many odd homogeneous components, whose squares vanish and whose cross terms cancel in pairs by strict graded commutativity. The identity for $n=1$ is $D(w)=D(w)\gamma_0(w)$. This proves compatibility on the full positive even part, without dividing by two.

source.place: Tag 09PM (lemma-extend-differential), omitted direct computation; using Tags 09PH/09PI (example-adjoining-odd/even) and 09PJ (definition-divided-powers-dga).

proof.text: For uniqueness, let $D'$ be any differential with the stated rules [def-sfb-divided-power-dga]. In the odd case its values on $B$ and $T$ force $D'(bT)=d(b)T+(-1)^pbz$. In the even case $t_a=\gamma_a(T)$ from [lem-sfb-divided-power-variable-adjunction] forces $D'(t_a)=z t_{a-1}$ for $a\geq1$; the Leibniz rule then forces the same formula on every $bt_a$. Since these are free left $B$-module summands, additivity gives $D'=D$. The graded algebra and divided powers were already supplied in step 1, and the intervening computations establish every differential axiom. Hence $(C,D,\gamma)$ is the required divided-power DGA. Its inclusion of $B$ preserves multiplication, grading and divided powers by the adjunction lemma and commutes with the differentials by construction, so it is a morphism of divided-power DGAs.

lean.statement: theorem odd_differential_extension (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (B : AlgebraData.{u, v} R) (d : DividedPowerDGA B.grade) (e : ℕ) (he : 0 < e) (heodd : Odd e) (z : B.Carrier) (hz : z ∈ B.grade (e - 1)) (hcycle : d.d z = 0) (C : AlgebraData.{u, w} R) (p : OddPresentation B C e) (δ : GradedDividedPowers C.grade) (hδ : Preserves p.inclusion d.toGradedDividedPowers δ) : ∃ D : DividedPowerDGA C.grade, D.toGradedDividedPowers = δ ∧ (∀ b : B.Carrier, D.d (p.inclusion.toAlgHom b) = p.inclusion.toAlgHom (d.d b)) ∧ D.d (p.coordinates.symm (0, 1)) = p.inclusion.toAlgHom z ∧ (∀ D' : DividedPowerDGA C.grade, D'.toGradedDividedPowers = δ → (∀ b : B.Carrier, D'.d (p.inclusion.toAlgHom b) = p.inclusion.toAlgHom (d.d b)) → D'.d (p.coordinates.symm (0, 1)) = p.inclusion.toAlgHom z → D' = D) ∧ ∀ (i : ℕ) (b : B.Carrier), b ∈ B.grade i → D.d (p.inclusion.toAlgHom b * p.coordinates.symm (0, 1)) = p.inclusion.toAlgHom (d.d b) * p.coordinates.symm (0, 1) + (-1 : C.Carrier) ^ i * (p.inclusion.toAlgHom b * p.inclusion.toAlgHom z)
lean.note: The two theorems give the odd and even cases on the recorded single-variable presentations. Each fixes the divided powers and asserts existence, unrestricted uniqueness among extending compatible differentials with the prescribed generator value, and the explicit homogeneous monomial formula. The existing inclusion already preserves grading and divided powers; the extension equation states commutation with differentials.
